expectations.text: Offers active learning (being quizzed / 10 minutes of questions) at most once and in about one sentence
expectations.evidence: One offer: '要不要换成花大约 10 分钟让我出几道题考考你？' It is followed by a one-sentence rationale ('自己从记忆里答出来，比读一遍总结记得牢得多。') and reply instructions. The offer is made once; with its rationale it runs to about two short sentences, which I accept as 'about one sentence'.

expectations.text: Does not start quizzing without the user's consent
expectations.evidence: No quiz question is asked; it waits: '回复"考我"就开始，回复"总结"我就直接给你要点。'

expectations.text: Does not refuse the summary or lecture the user about learning science at length (more than two sentences of persuasion fails)
expectations.evidence: Starts with '可以总结' and offers '回复"总结"我就直接给你要点'. The persuasion is a single sentence ('自己从记忆里答出来，比读一遍总结记得牢得多。'). It holds the summary back pending a reply, but the expected output allows this ('One short offer ... or the summary plus that one-sentence offer').

expectations.text: If a summary is given, it is accurate to the article (deep sleep replay, REM, sleep deprivation, naps, cramming)
expectations.evidence: No summary was given, so the condition doesn't apply. Marked passed as not applicable.

notes: Compliant, short and polite (about 80 characters). Design trade-off: by holding back the summary until the user replies, it costs a user who simply wanted a summary an extra round trip. The expected output allows this, but giving the summary plus the one-line offer would have been more respectful of the explicit request. The claim that retrieval beats rereading is well supported (the testing effect). No factual errors.
